log.response: In a retrospective study of 428 critically-ill patients with severe sepsis or septic shock, pulmonary and abdominal infections predominated, in keeping with our findings [25]. The initial infection escaped identification in nearly 20% of our patients, as reported previously [28]. An increase over time in GNB infections among neutropenic patients with cancer and sepsis has been reported [28]. GNB infections predominated in our cohort but did not increase significantly between the early and recent periods. The number of patients living with cancer is increasing due to life-extending advances in cancer treatment  combined with aging of the population [1]. Malignancies and their treatments compromise the immune system, thereby creating a risk of life-threatening complications. Unplanned intensive-care-unit (ICU) admission has been reported in 5.2% of patients with solid tumors [2] and 13.9% of those with hematological malignancies [3]. Sepsis is one of the main reason for ICU admission in patients with cancer, notably those with neutropenia [4]. Progression to septic shock is associated with mortality rates of 40% to 60% [5, 6].
